result:
**The plan.** The read-only agent guard found each subcommand's command by walking past leading keywords, assignments and prefix utilities, then taking the first remaining word. It made only one guess. If that word was something zsh might treat as a prefix, the real mutator after it went unread. Eight recorded bypasses came through this gap: leading `{` or `[[ … ]]`, zsh `=cmd`, and assignments the regex missed. The plan was to read such words both ways and deny if either reading denies, without letting anything through that was denied before.

**The build.** `_stop_index` is the old walk, now able to start at any position and use a memo. `_command_starts` builds on it. It yields the original candidate first, then queues extra walks at ambiguous stop words: after `{`, after each later `]]`, after a word containing `=`, and with leading `=` stripped. `_classify_subcommand` checks every candidate, and the first denial wins. Because a slow hook fails open, four bounds keep the walk linear, plus a fail-closed cap of 64 candidates. Those bounds are visited pairs, a queued set, a stop on the `[[` scan, and the memo. New tests cover denials, allows, the cap and work growth.

**The project.** The guard now denies a strict superset of what it denied before, and all eight bypasses are closed. The cost is a small accepted class of false positives and a new cap message. A sweep of 150,024 real commands found no new false positives. The README, spec, plan, history and deferred items are updated. Gate B, the post-merge probe, still has to be run, because the hook goes live everywhere on merge.
